children: The latest National Hurricane Center update at 11 a.m. ET Tuesday showed stronger winds for Tropical Storm Edouard as the storm moves closer to the Texas coast.

The storm was about 30 miles south of Cameron, La., and about 50 miles southeast of Port Arthur, Texas, and had sustained winds of 50 mph as of the latest NHC update. The system is still moving northwest at about 8 mph. A Category 1 hurricane has a minimum sustained wind speed of 74 mph.

Current watches remained unchanged, with a storm surge warning in affect from High Island, Texas, to the Vermilion/Cameron Parish line in Louisiana, a hurricane watch in effect from High Island, Texas, to Cameron, La., and a larger area of the Gulf Coast, from Port Bolivar, Texas, to the Vermilion/Iberia Parish line, still under a tropical storm warning.

The latest NHC release says the storm is expected to continue to strengthen as it nears the coast, with tropical storm force winds still expected to extend up to 25 miles from the center of the storm. However, the NHC expects "rapid weakening after the center moves inland."

Tropical storm conditions will spread over the warning area in the next few hours, said the NHC's most recent release, with storm surges between 3-5 feet for High Island to Vermilion/Cameron Parish line, and 1-3 feet of storm surge from the Vermilion/Cameron Parish line to Morgan City, La.
Rainfall totals of 3-6 inches are expected, with maximum estimates near 9 inches for the upper Texas Coast inland through east-central Texas, with 2-4 inches expected in far southwest Louisiana.
NHC will release another advisory at 2 p.m. ET with updated storm information.
As of publication time, there have been no reports of refinery closures or rampdowns and little storm impact on Gulf Coast spot market trading.
